claims.text: Near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles can be synthesized by a one-pot colloidal or solvothermal method.
The as-synthesized HEA nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The as-synthesized HEA nanoparticles form a single solid-solution phase.
Configurational entropy favors a single solid-solution phase over intermetallic formation or phase segregation in HEAs.
Lattice distortion in HEAs arises from differences in the atomic sizes of their constituent elements.
Severe lattice distortion causes low atomic diffusivity in HEAs.
The magnitude of lattice distortion governs the high-temperature structural and chemical stability of near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticles.
Adding a trace, size-mismatched element to a near-equiatomic HEA nanoparticle increases its lattice distortion.
The trace-modified composition has increased configurational entropy relative to the baseline composition.
Reduced atomic mobility limits elemental segregation and phase separation at high temperature.
Diffusion suppression preserves uniform nanoparticle composition and structure during high-temperature service.
Trace-modified nanoparticles will show less phase separation than the baseline nanoparticles.
Trace-modified nanoparticles will retain a more homogeneous elemental distribution than the baseline nanoparticles.
Trace-modified nanoparticles will preserve catalytic or thermoelectric performance better than the baseline under elevated temperatures.
The baseline near-equiatomic HEA composition possesses inherent lattice distortion.
Above a temperature threshold, thermal energy overwhelms stabilization associated with lattice distortion.
Excessive addition of the size-mismatched element can produce secondary phases or undesired intermetallic compounds.
There may be an optimal concentration of the size-mismatched element that maximizes stability without inducing destabilizing phase changes.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes lattice distortion as configurational-entropy-induced, whereas the structural mediator and cited HEA evidence attribute lattice distortion to atomic-size mismatch. The mechanism otherwise treats configurational entropy and lattice distortion as separate effects.
